clue.text: Rump, ham or game?

parts.note: the rump of an animal is its back end, so back
gammon is a cured ham from the hind leg of a pig

explanation.surface: A butcher's query about which cut of meat or game to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists meats, so 'game' looks like venison or pheasant; it is the definition, a board game. GAMMON is British cured pork.
explanation.definitionFit: This board game, played with dice and counters, is among the oldest pastimes known.

clue.text: Exhausted ticket seller after sting

indicators.note: after places the ticket seller below the sting word in this down answer

parts.note: to sting is to burn, as nettles do
a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A ticket seller worn out after being caught in a sting operation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' suggests a police trap on the tout, but it means BURN. A tout is a British ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: Burnt-out means exhausted from overwork or stress.

clue.text: Insurance agent's final secret

parts.note: insurance cover is the protection a policy gives

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of agent's, ignoring the possessive s

explanation.surface: An insurance agent's last confidential matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means concealed or done in secret, as in covert operations.

clue.text: 'Shot' — small drink for small talk

parts.note: to have a shot is to have a go
a sip is a small drink

explanation.surface: Ordering a shot, a tiny drink, while chatting idly at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' looks like a measure of spirits beside 'drink', but means GO, an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip is idle chatter about others, a form of small talk.

clue.text: Doctor performing easy work unofficially

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
on stage means performing, so on
light work is easy work

explanation.surface: A doctor taking on easy work on the side without permission.
explanation.definitionFit: To moonlight is to hold a second job, often secretly or off the books.

clue.text: They open, exceptionally, for a new convert

indicators.note: exceptionally means in an unusual way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shops open on an unusual basis to welcome a recent convert.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a beginner, originally someone newly baptised into a faith.

clue.text: Slump preceding a long tale

indicators.note: preceding says the slump word comes before the a in the answer

parts.note: to slump is to sag or droop

explanation.surface: A dull narrative where the story slumps before a lengthy tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A Norse family epic, by extension any lengthy rambling story, is a long tale.

clue.text: Drink on board with partner's representative

indicators.note: on board means aboard a ship, so the drink sits inside the steamship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, and the convention on board means inside SS
ale is a drink, a kind of beer
man is a partner, as in man and wife; the possessive s is ignored

explanation.surface: Having a drink aboard ship with one's partner's agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the crossword convention for going inside SS (steamship).
explanation.definitionFit: A sales representative, or rep, is a salesman for a company.

clue.text: Go to Scotland and put up new fuel nerve centre

parts.note: gang is Scots for go

indicators.note: put up in a down answer means the following letters are written upwards, read reversed

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: Instructions to head to Scotland and install a fresh fuel supply at headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, literally a nerve centre.

clue.text: Fine-tuning of foresight on unloaded rifle

indicators.note: on places the next piece directly after the emptied rifle in this across answer
unloaded means emptied of its contents, leaving only the outside letters of the word rifle

parts.note: foresight is vision, the ability to see ahead

explanation.surface: Adjusting the foresight, the front sight, on a rifle with no ammunition in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A foresight is genuinely part of a rifle, so the surface reads as gunsmithing; here it means VISION.
explanation.definitionFit: A revision is an amendment or improvement, which is what fine-tuning amounts to.

clue.text: The shape of Bologna after most of it is developed

indicators.note: developed means grown or worked into a new form, so the remaining letters are rearranged
most of it means the word Bologna loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Describing how the Italian city of Bologna has been built up over time.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last A of Bologna leaves BOLOGN, which 'is developed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: This rectangle with unequal sides is a geometrical figure, hence a shape.

clue.text: Work land area on hill producing food for Mexico

indicators.note: on puts the tilled area beside the hill, coming after it in this across answer

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
to till is to work land by ploughing

explanation.surface: A farmer cultivating a hillside plot to grow Mexican food.
explanation.definitionFit: This thin flatbread of maize or wheat is a staple of Mexican cooking.

clue.text: Swindle crowd

definitions.meaning: to swindle or con someone, as a verb or a noun for a con
to crowd or jostle, push roughly

explanation.definitionFit: A con trick is a swindle, and to jostle or push past people is to crowd them.

clue.text: Smile, with time for new determination

indicators.note: time for new says the letter for time replaces the letter for new

parts.note: a grin is a broad smile

explanation.surface: Advice to keep smiling and take time to find fresh resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: Grit is courage and resolve, a dogged strength of character.

clue.text: Inflexible but viable perhaps including two thousand plus order initially

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters may be arranged in some other way, signalling an anagram

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of order

explanation.surface: Something rigid yet workable that includes a large sum and an order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Including' and 'plus' just join the pieces of the pool that 'perhaps' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Immovable means fixed and unyielding, so inflexible.

clue.text: Done half of this part of the golf course

indicators.note: half of takes the first two of the four letters of the word this

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway on a golf course

explanation.surface: A golfer who has finished half the course in the long grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To be through is to have finished, so done, as in 'I'm through with this'.

clue.text: Fine line taken in joint request for small container

indicators.note: taken in means the two short letters are placed inside the joint and request

parts.note: the hip is a joint of the body
to ask is to request
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Asking a joint for fine linen for a little box.
explanation.definitionFit: A hip flask is a small flat bottle for spirits, carried in a pocket.

clue.text: Lack of love on religious outpost?

indicators.note: on places the love letter above the outpost in this down answer

parts.note: love means nil in tennis, the letter O
a mission is a religious station in a remote place

explanation.surface: A remote mission without love, asked as a question.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is something left out, so a lack or failure to include.

clue.text: Good Independent newspaper report for retail outlet

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
to shop someone is British slang for informing on them to the police

explanation.surface: A good independent newspaper reports on a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Independent and the FT are both real British papers, so the surface reads as press talk; SHOP means to inform on.
explanation.definitionFit: A gift shop is a store selling presents and souvenirs, a retail outlet.

clue.text: Import from Chinese dynasty to include endless jeans

indicators.note: to include means the dynasty's name holds the trimmed jeans inside it

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644

indicators.note: endless means the word jeans loses both its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A trader importing jeans from China, oddly linked to a historic dynasty.
explanation.definitionFit: Import in the sense of significance or sense, as in 'the import of his words'.

clue.text: Coins once used for drugs lie all over the place

indicators.note: all over the place means scattered in disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Old coins used to buy drugs strewn everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The guilder was the Dutch currency before the euro, so these are former coins.

clue.text: Piece of news one came across on the way back

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: on the way back means the word for came across is read in reverse

parts.note: came across someone means met them

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a person they bumped into while returning home.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is a single report or story in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Fashionable channel to admit as member

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a duct is a channel or tube

explanation.surface: A trendy TV channel admitting someone into its club.
explanation.definitionFit: To induct someone is to formally admit them to an office or organisation.

clue.text: Country or kingdom raised women on island

indicators.note: on places the women letter above the island in this down answer
raised in a down answer means the letters are written upwards, read in reverse

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom
an ait is a small island in a river

explanation.surface: A nation or kingdom where women were elevated on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: AIT, a small river island, is common in British usage on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Kuwait is a Gulf state, an independent country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Nothing very loud to establish counterbalance

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud
to set something up is to establish it

explanation.surface: Making a lot of noise out of nothing in order to set up a balance.
explanation.definitionFit: To offset is to compensate for or balance one thing against another.

clue.text: Net value is adjusted, becoming final after a time

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or reset, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An accountant's note that a net figure will be finalised after a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means ultimately occurring, coming at the end once time has passed.

clue.text: Chair apparently embracing return of outcast

indicators.note: return of means that run is taken backwards
embracing means the two words hold the run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A committee chair seemingly welcoming back someone who had been shunned.
explanation.definitionFit: A pariah is a social reject, someone shunned and excluded by others.

clue.text: Stubborn, but bound to reform without new charge

indicators.note: reform means reshape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
without says the letter for new is dropped from the word bound

parts.note: a rate is a charge or fee

explanation.surface: An unrepentant person, certain to change once a new fee is waived.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing N from BOUND leaves BOUD, which 'to reform' shuffles into OBDU.
explanation.definitionFit: Obdurate means stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion, hence obstinate.

clue.text: Hide, if virtually broke

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: skint is British slang for broke, with no money

explanation.surface: Someone advised to hide away when nearly out of money.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is everyday British slang for penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's hide is its skin, the noun being the same thing.

clue.text: People in power panicking at teens on grass

indicators.note: on places the rearranged letters after the slang word in this across answer

parts.note: grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

indicators.note: panicking means thrown into confusion, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Those in authority alarmed at teenagers smoking cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Potentates are rulers or monarchs, people wielding great power.
